target: Reader public landing and capture-to-reading entry

customReplacement.reason: The landing uses semantic Astro sections, native details disclosures, links, and buttons; no standard interactive control was rebuilt.

contract.purpose: Help a serious reader move saved articles and PDFs out of tabs and bookmarks into a focused place to read, annotate, question, revisit, and retrieve them.
contract.purposeSource: PROJECT_STATUS.md, repository routes, public agent surfaces, and current capture-to-reading implementation
contract.canonicalPurpose: Reader is a maintained personal research library for capturing article URLs and PDFs, reading them closely, marking and discussing useful passages, and finding the material again later.
contract.audience: Serious readers whose saved research is fragmented across browser tabs, bookmarks, and files; browser-local use is available without an account and an account-backed library is available through Google sign-in.
contract.job: Explain the capture-to-reading loop, demonstrate the reading workspace, and disclose account, privacy, extension, and commercial boundaries before asking the visitor to open Reader.
contract.thesis: A warm editorial research desk should make the product feel like a place for thinking, not another generic read-later inbox.
contract.system: Warm paper and ink, restrained rust accent, serif editorial headlines, compact utility labels, fine rules, a purpose-built reading-workspace illustration, and a responsive single-column collapse on narrow screens.
contract.signature: The first viewport pairs the capture-to-use promise with a detailed Reader workspace showing source metadata, notes, questions, and retrieval context.
contract.risk: The page is text-rich by design, but exact 390, 768, and 1440 CSS-pixel captures preserve hierarchy, scannability, actions, and zero horizontal overflow.

projectCheck.command: pnpm typecheck && pnpm exec vitest run src/agent-surfaces.test.ts src/lib/spa-route.test.ts && pnpm cf:build && pnpm docs:check

findings: No product-purpose, hierarchy, contrast, interaction, responsive, or overflow P0/P1 finding remains in the candidate.

The five link-graph orphan candidates are deliberate application or utility routes: library, sample, and login are task entry points; about and privacy are client-rendered app pages. None is falsely presented as an indexable marketing page.

answers.product: A personal research library for saved articles and PDFs.
answers.audience: People who save serious reading but lose it across tabs, bookmarks, and files.
answers.value: Saved sources become usable working knowledge rather than an unread queue.
answers.mechanism: Capture a URL or PDF, read in a focused workspace, mark and question passages, then retrieve the source and its context later.
answers.proof: The hero demonstrates the real reading workspace and the next sections walk through the four-step loop, current capabilities, access paths, privacy boundaries, and source-built extension state.
answers.nextAction: Open the browser-local Reader, try a sample document, or sign in with Google for the account-backed library; there is no checkout.

ownerFeedback.note: The owner delegated end-to-end landing repair and qualification in SaaSMaker priority order and asked not to pause for routine feedback. Production release remains outside this local audit.
